newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic, Nynex deny report of 10,000 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic, Nynex deny report of 10,000 job cuts.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp. and Nynex Corp. Tuesday denied a published report that they planned to cut at least 10,000 jobs after completing their merger.

The companies said they planned to cut 3,000 management positions within three years, as previously announced. The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the plan, reported that the companies were likely to cut 10,000 jobs or more within five years after the merger.

The newspaper quoted the sources as saying that while no hard number of cuts had been set, depending on how quickly the companies can consolidate back-room operations, 15,000 jobs or more might eventually be eliminated.
"Anyone who thinks we're going to stop at 15,000 is either naive or doing a lot of wishful thinking," the newspaper quoted one executive as saying.
The newspaper said people familiar with the plan said it was "reasonable" that at least 10,000 jobs would be cut within five years.
In a four-paragraph statement, Bell Atlantic and Nynex said they had no plans for any cuts other than the 3,000 already announced.
Citing the Wall Street Journal's story referring to possible larger cuts, the companies said, "There are no such plans."

The companies have a combined total of about 137,000 employees. The Journal story said the original estimate of 3,000 cuts was deliberately conservative to avoid arousing criticism such as AT&T Corp. received when it announced plans to cut 40,000 jobs as part of its breakup.
The Bell Atlantic-Nynex merger, announced in April 1996, will form the nation's biggest local phone company.

The companies said in their statement that they will respond to competition by cutting costs and improving efficiency, and added that some parts of Bell Atlantic's business were adding employees to meet new opportunities.
The Justice Department approved the merger last month. A decision by Federal Communications Commission is pending.
Bell Atlantic stock rose 12.5 cents to $69.25 and Nynex added 25 cents to $52.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
